devices.name: Moog Music Memorymoog
devices.tagline: Six-voice analog polysynth with 18 oscillators and patch memory, made from 1982 to 1985

entries.name: KRACHT
entries.summary: Hard techno drum machine built with the VIBE FM SDK: a synthesised kick designer with seven presets, a rumble made from the kick, hats, clap and a 16-step sequencer; no samples. It runs in the VIBE FM player and plugin…

entries.name: A22
entries.summary: FM workstation for the FM-1, derived from h1: ten synth and drum engines with eight algorithms each, eight effects, a four-track tape with knob automation, a mixer, Riff and Shake sequencers and chord memory.

entries.name: Bloomy
entries.summary: Groovebox firmware for the FM-1 derived from LOOM-8, with five project slots, per-track generator, evolver and Turing functions, Knit and Jacquard engines with a chorus, and Italian-language offline tools for backup, so…

entries.name: CHORD RUN
entries.summary: One-finger chord player for the FM-1 with 17 song sets, a scale-matched melody on the white keys, drum styles, a 4-bar looper and a runner game that scores your playing. Rights warning: the song sets use the chords of c…

entries.name: Chordism
entries.summary: Chord synth for the FM-1, a port of the Chordism Schwung module: each key plays a four-voice chord with morphing levels and pans, FM, a pressure-controlled filter, lo-fi, delay, plate reverb and an arpeggiator.

entries.name: Floop Studio
entries.summary: FL Studio plugin (VST3 and AU, macOS) with a four-track MIDI step sequencer and a live editor for an FM-1 running SLOOP: pattern, sounds, sample upload, MIDI map and two-way clock.

entries.name: FM1-800
entries.summary: Fan-made Korg Poly-800 for the FM-1 with its 64 factory programs plus 64 user slots, Poly-800 style editing, chorus and a 256-note step sequencer, and an added phaser, tape echo, high-pass and MIDI clock in. Rights warn…

entries.name: FM-1 Pocket Player
entries.summary: Browser player that runs FM-1 community firmware on an on-screen panel, with a searchable library of firmware from The Firmware Hub, original .fwsc packages on an FM-1 chip emulator and .rfm1 builds on a simulator, and…

entries.name: FM1-RDX
entries.summary: Four-operator FM synth for the FM-1 inspired by the Yamaha Reface DX: 33 sounds, twelve algorithms, up to eight adaptive voices, two of seven effects and Reface-style SysEx, with a browser emulator.

entries.name: GhettoMachine
entries.summary: Four-track groovebox for the FM-1: a 909 or 808 drum track, three mono, poly or sampler tracks, a 64-step sequencer with 16 patterns, a scene grid, a 303 pattern generator and per-track stems over USB.

entries.name: KALK
entries.summary: Beat composer for the FM-1 after the workflow of Limelite: five synthesised drum and tone voices, a three-lane sequence in four patterns, looping side lanes, 127 remix variations, an XY effect with recorded motion and a…

entries.name: KO BASS
entries.summary: Bass-line firmware for the FM-1: the KO genre engine narrowed to bass, with Acid, Sub, Reese, FM, Fold and Sync eras, LINE presets with user plates, and tempo and clock tools.

entries.name: KO FM-1 player
entries.summary: GitHub Pages browser player and Web MIDI installer for the KO firmwares: runs each of the fifteen as WebAssembly with an on-screen FM-1 and installs its package on a connected unit from Chrome or Edge.

entries.name: KO genre firmwares
entries.summary: Twelve genre firmwares for the FM-1 built on one shared engine and Dinghy: DUB, HOUSE, HVYPSY, JAZZ, IDM, HIPHOP, POP, FUNK, TECHNO, TRIPHOP, SOUL and XCRASH, each with its own plates and installed as its own package.

entries.name: KO JET
entries.summary: Work-in-progress synth and sequencer firmware for the FM-1 with its own engine, banks, preset-like patches and a new sequencer with recording; the README says it has run only in the simulator and emulator, not on hardwa…

entries.name: KO KIT
entries.summary: Drum firmware for the FM-1 with sixteen synthesised drum voices, eleven performance pads, groove plates across kit eras and its own sequencer and store; it is not one of the genre packs.

entries.name: Loom CAFA
entries.summary: Experimental fork of the Android app LOOM Groovebox that uses an FM-1 running Windjammer as its controller, display and USB audio output, with the eight LOOM tracks selectable from the FM-1.

entries.name: Sillage
entries.summary: Eight-track groovebox for the FM-1 derived from Skiff and Felucca, with 448 presets sorted by family, a 64-step sequencer with SONG, scenes and PERFORM modes, a 4-band EQ per track and a stereo master stage.

entries.name: Viber
entries.summary: Six-track groovebox for the FM-1 derived from Skiff and Felucca, adding a wavetable engine, a two-page clips mode, round knob displays and a master level meter.

entries.name: Volna
entries.summary: Wavetable synth for the FM-1 built on Dinghy: three oscillators per voice, two filters, four envelopes, a modulation matrix, effects and a step arpeggiator with its own pattern for every patch.

entries.name: KNOBI-SIX
entries.summary: Standalone OB-6-inspired polysynth for the SMK-37 Pro: six voices, two oscillators, a state-variable filter, the front panel's 12 knobs, patch memory, an arpeggiator and clock, distortion and a step sequencer.

entries.name: sloop-fm1-tab5
entries.summary: Port of the SLOOP groovebox engine to the Tab5 with a touchscreen UI and Tab5 Keyboard input, in development on the dev branch of the repository, with a planned companion mode for an FM-1 over USB.

entries.name: Enaga
entries.summary: Unofficial replacement firmware for the SmplTrek that runs apps written in C++ from the SD card, with a DSP library, file, MIDI and clock services and a synth example. Update files are also built for the Lofi-12 XT and…

DATA is the page's own knob: it sets only the sounds on SOUND, the list, step or pedal where there is one, the level on MIXER, and on other pages the card marked DATA.
Fixes the mixer needles, track level lines and pad lights sticking at the loudest moment, and the idle screen's figure grows anew each bar and flares on hits.
The idle screen draws discharges from its corners, top, sides and floor on drum hits, and on their own in silence.
HAUNT's picture follows the bar's real snare and clap hits, and on DRAG a dot rides the tape's speed.

A pulse of current runs through the figure behind the pages on every hit, unless SCREEN WEAR is off, and MASTER shows WEAR as a column of cells.
RETURN goes back to the page before, step by step, DATA walks the lists of PROJECTS, FILES, PARTS A-D and MY SOUNDS, and in the plugin and Playground a click on the DATA knob is ENTER.
SHIFT + HOME opens MENU, which is always at the top of the display, and a click on DATA is ENTER.
